phases.name: Slice 01: A neighbourhood for every rung of the property ladder
phases.description: Builds on the walking skeleton: BANNER_TIME moves to config.js; a pure plan says which neighbourhood each frame shows and how far the next has faded in; the recipes paint on a context they are handed; a store of two, with its fail-safe, and a shell that render.js only calls replace the skeleton's cache and fade; the arrival sentence names the neighbourhood; two road colours are darkened so that everything stays readable. Ends with no @pending, no RED scaffold, and the Rendering universe checked by hand.

steps.name: BANNER_TIME moves to the game's timing constants
criteria: BANNER_TIME, 2.4 s, is declared once, in src/game/config.js beside STEP and MAX_FRAME; game.js imports it and re-exports it, and keeps no value of its own.
Every existing import of BANNER_TIME from game.js still works and reads 2.4: render.js, the fanfare-length unit check and the in-memory harness's copy of the rules.
The seventh layering rule holds: view/backdrop.js imports only from theme/ and game/config.js, and its broken case, importing BANNER_TIME from game.js, is still reported.
No scenario is enabled and nothing the game does changes: the unit and in-memory projects pass as before.
steps.scenario_name: src and netlify keep the seven layering rules of ADR-006, ADR-009 and ADR-010 | no stretch of the fanfare, up to any note, outlasts the Wave cleared banner
steps.implementation_notes: DDD-B5 and DDD-B15 (H-1, F9; the user's decision): DELIVER's first step, so the plan can take the banner time under the seventh rule. Declare BANNER_TIME = 2.4 in src/game/config.js beside STEP and MAX_FRAME, moving its comment with it (seconds the 'Wave cleared!' banner shows; the fanfare must fit inside it). game.js (line 19) imports it from ./config.js and re-exports it; its own use at line 410 is untouched. render.js (line 4), tests/unit/fanfare-length.spec.js and the in-memory harness (rules.BANNER_TIME on a fresh copy of game.js) keep importing it from game.js unchanged. backdrop.js doesn't import it yet: the plan does in 01-03. The game/ layering rule already allows game.js to import ./config.js. Enables no scenario: of DISTILL's 55 @pending runs, none depends on this move. EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: a constant moves, with no behaviour to state as a property. Compensate with the property-based test at unit level on the adjacent slot: fanfare-length.spec.js's fast-check property, which reads BANNER_TIME through the re-export. DONE WHEN: npm run build is green (bddgen, the unit and in-memory projects, then the dist copy; H1), and the walking skeleton is green in all three engines: npx playwright test --project=chromium --project=firefox --project=webkit --grep "Clearing the first wave". ALSO DONE WHEN (L2): grep -nE 'BANNER_TIME *=' src/game/*.js finds config.js only.

steps.name: The backdrop plan: which neighbourhood each screen shows
criteria: The title and a game just started show City centre at dawn, with nothing fading in.

In play, with a home lost and at game over, the backdrop is the neighbourhood of the rung reached, with nothing fading in: Terraced streets in the morning once the first wave's banner ends or a home is lost on the second wave, Countryside at sunset at game over on the fifth.
Playing again from a higher rung shows City centre at dawn at once, with no fade.
The plan answers from the frame it is handed alone (its level, state and banner), whatever the pause, and changes nothing it is handed.
steps.scenario_name: The title shows the city centre at dawn, with nothing fading in | Starting a game keeps the city centre at dawn, with nothing fading in | When the banner ends, I am in the next neighbourhood, with nothing fading in | Losing a home fades nothing in | The game-over screen shows the neighbourhood I reached | Playing again from a higher rung goes straight back to the city centre at dawn

In this step here = neighbourhood(level), next = null and mix = 0 for title, play, dead and over; 'clear' is 01-03's, and its scenarios are that step's RED. The steps hand the plan a frozen { level, state, banner, paused }: read only the first three, ignore paused, write nothing. backdrop.js still imports only theme/ and game/config.js (the seventh rule). render.js doesn't call the plan until 01-05, so the game is unchanged. steps.name: The backdrop plan: the next neighbourhood fades in while Wave cleared! shows
criteria: On the first 'Wave cleared!' frame the next rung's neighbourhood is named over the one being left, at a strength of 0%.

The strength is the share of the 2.4 s banner gone, to within a twentieth of a percent: 25%, 50%, 75% and 97.9% after 0.6, 1.2, 1.8 and 2.35 s, and 50% half way through the banner on each of the first five waves.
For a banner the game never reaches, the strength holds at its ends: 100% with -0.5 s left, 0% with 3 s left.
From Forever home onwards, on the sixth, seventh and tenth waves, nothing fades in while 'Wave cleared!' shows.
Pausing for 10 s mid-fade holds the fade at 50%; the plan takes the banner time from game/config.js, never from the rules.

steps.name: Each neighbourhood painted on a context it is handed; Forever home's cottage moved
criteria: Every neighbourhood paints in full on a context it is handed, in game units, without setting a transform or asking for anything the context doesn't offer.
Painting never reaches for Math.random, and painting a neighbourhood twice makes the same calls in the same order.
Every fill and stroke is one of the neighbourhood's palette colours, or COLORS.green for the ground line, with its streets in its road colour and its skyline in its sky colour.
The game keeps drawing every neighbourhood through these same recipes, which exist once in backdrop.js.

Forever home's cottage, with its roof and lit window, lies clear of the houses' x ranges (84-156, 324-396, 564-636, 804-876), by its coordinates; the visual pass test of every landmark is 01-10's by-hand check.
steps.scenario_name: Drawing every neighbourhood leaves the game's luck alone | Every neighbourhood is drawn exactly the same way every time | Every neighbourhood is drawn only in its own colours, and the green of the ground line | Every neighbourhood has its streets and its skyline
steps.implementation_notes: DISTILL's handoff step 3. DDD-B1 and DDD-B2: paintBackdrop(context, neighbourhood) paints on the context it is handed, in game units. It paints the palette's bg over 0, 0, W, H, then the look's map, the look's skyline and the green ground line (COLORS.green, 0, GROUND, W, 2). It uses the rung's own mulberry32, seeded with 1000 + its index in NEIGHBOURHOODS. It sets no transform: the painting context doesn't offer setTransform, and refuses it. The store will set the scale before it paints (01-05). It may use only the calls the recipes make today (PAINT_CALLS in tests/unit/support/fake-canvas.js). buildBackdrop keeps the game drawing until 01-05 deletes it. Meanwhile it only creates, sizes and scales a canvas and hands that canvas's context to paintBackdrop, so the recipes exist once. Never move the houses. The lighthouse (x 298-322) already stands clear. M3 then checks that the moved art is still palette-only and seeded; the other landmarks are checked by hand in 01-10. steps.name: The store and the shell, with render.js only calling them
criteria: A neighbourhood shown for 10 s is prepared once, at the game's size (1920 by 1440 at double size), and scaled to that size before anything is painted on it.
The store keeps the two neighbourhoods asked for last, dropping the least recently asked-for first, and never prepares again one that it holds at its size.
The shell draws the neighbourhood underneath at full strength over the whole screen, then the one fading in at the fade's strength, asking for it even at 0%, and leaves the strength as it found it.

Over a climb to the seventh wave, each neighbourhood is prepared only as it first appears: City centre at dawn as the title appears, and each next one as 'Wave cleared!' first appears. A new game after the climb prepares City centre at dawn once more.

render.js only calls showBackdrop(ctx, backdropPlan({ level, state, banner }), store.canvasFor), with the frame read from g, at the start of draw(). It creates the store with () => document.createElement('canvas'), its resize() calls rescale(k), and it has no cache or fade logic left.
buildBackdrop, the skeleton's cache code in render.js and the RED-scaffold marker are deleted: no old path coexists with the new one.
The walking skeleton stays green in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.
steps.scenario_name: A neighbourhood is prepared once, however long it is shown | The screen keeps the two neighbourhoods it showed last | When the screen <trouble>, I see <underneath>, with <over it> | Over a whole climb, each neighbourhood is prepared only as it first appears | Playing again after a long climb prepares the city centre at dawn once more, as the new game starts
steps.implementation_notes: DISTILL's handoff step 4 enables 8 scenarios (9 runs), so it is split. This step covers the store, the shell and render.js on them; the same-scale rule is 01-06's. They can't be split from each other: every M4 scenario draws through the real shell over the real store. DDD-B3, DDD-B5 (F7, M-3, N8, L-4b). THE STORE: createBackdropCache(createCanvas) returns { rescale(k), canvasFor(neighbourhood) }. canvasFor builds a backdrop the first time it is asked for one. It takes a canvas from createCanvas() (called with no arguments) and sizes it round(W * k) by round(H * k). The 2D context's first call is setTransform(k, 0, 0, k, 0, 0), and paintBackdrop follows. canvasFor moves the neighbourhood to most recent and keeps at most two, dropping the least recently asked-for. Both methods must work detached, since render.js hands store.canvasFor to the shell unbound (closures, as the skeleton's cache uses). In this step, rescale(k) sets the scale and drops every canvas, as the skeleton's cache does; the early return on the same scale is 01-06's. A canvas that can't be built is 01-07's. THE SHELL: showBackdrop(context, plan, canvasFor) asks canvasFor for here, then for next whenever the plan names one, even at mix 0. That is why the next rung is built on the first 'Wave cleared!' frame, which the climb scenario checks. It draws here's canvas over 0, 0, W, H at full strength, then next's at globalAlpha = mix, then puts globalAlpha back as it found it. The screen's recording offers only drawImage, fillRect, save and restore, plus fillStyle and globalAlpha. RENDER.JS (L1, in one edit, so no name is declared twice): delete its own backdrop cache and fade (the createBackdropCache and drawBackdrop functions), and the BANNER_TIME and neighbourhood imports only they used. Add const store = createBackdropCache(() => document.createElement('canvas')). draw() starts with showBackdrop(ctx, backdropPlan({ level: g.level, state: g.state, banner: g.banner }), store.canvasFor), and resize() ends with store.rescale(k). main.js is unchanged: it already calls resize() at load and on every window resize. Delete buildBackdrop from backdrop.js: canvases now come only from the factory. With the last scaffold body gone, delete `export const __SCAFFOLD__ = true` and the RED-scaffold header comment too (L6), rewording any unit comment that still speaks of scaffolds. COMPOSITION OUTLINE: move its @pending from the outline onto its @error Examples block. That enables the first block's 2 runs (here ok, next none or ok); 01-07 enables the rest. Today these scenarios fail at the When or at an arranging Given, on the store's RED scaffold. Then make it pass and delete its @pending, one at a time. Change no step, driver, helper or scenario text. steps.name: Only a change of scale prepares the backdrops again
criteria: A resize that keeps the game's size prepares nothing again: the neighbourhoods on screen keep the backdrops they have.
A resize to a new size prepares each neighbourhood on screen once more, at the new size (2880 by 2160 at triple size).
A resize half way through 'Wave cleared!' prepares both the neighbourhood being left and the one fading in once more, at the new size.

'Resizing the window without changing the game's size keeps...' is this step's RED. steps.name: A backdrop that can't be prepared shows its plain background, and the game plays on
criteria: When the screen has no room for a backdrop, or loses its drawing part-way through one, that neighbourhood shows its plain background over the whole screen and the game plays on: nothing is thrown to the game, nothing is reported, and nothing is asked of the screen that it doesn't offer.

The composition table's four failing rows draw as it says: a neighbourhood that couldn't be prepared is a fill in its palette's bg, at the strength its backdrop would have had, and no image is ever drawn from a backdrop that failed.

When the title's backdrop can't be prepared, City centre at dawn shows its plain background, and a game still starts at Studio flat, saying only 'Game started. Defend your dream home from the hurdles.'
A backdrop that couldn't be prepared doesn't stop the next one: Terraced streets in the morning shows its plain background, and Suburbs at midday its backdrop.
steps.scenario_name: When the screen <trouble>, I see <underneath>, with <over it> | When the screen <trouble>, the neighbourhood shows its plain background and the game plays on | The title's backdrop can't be prepared, and the game still starts and plays | A backdrop that couldn't be prepared doesn't stop the next one
steps.implementation_notes: DISTILL's handoff step 5 enables 8 scenarios (12 runs), so it is split at DDD-B4's own seam. This step covers what a failed build shows; how long the failure is remembered is 01-08's. DDD-B4, and DDD-B5's null guard (the composition table's failing rows). A build fails when getContext('2d') returns null, or when a call throws while the canvas is sized, scaled or painted. canvasFor then returns null for that neighbourhood, throws nothing and writes nothing to the console. Catch only around the build: a built canvas is assumed not to throw when drawn (Catalogued lies), and a wider catch would hide rendering bugs. THE SHELL: for a null canvas it calls fillRect(0, 0, W, H) in that neighbourhood's palette.bg, at the strength its canvas would have had (full for here, mix for next), and never calls drawImage(null). globalAlpha is put back as before. In this step a failed neighbourhood may be built again the next time it is asked for: remembering failures is 01-08's. steps.name: The arrival sentence names the neighbourhood
criteria: Moving up to each of the second to sixth waves, a screen reader hears 'Wave cleared! Moving up the ladder to {rung}.', then 'Now on the property ladder at {rung}. {Neighbourhood}.', for example 'Now on the property ladder at Terrace. Terraced streets in the morning.'
From Forever home onwards it is heard at the start of every wave: 'Now on the property ladder at Forever home. Seaside at night.' on the seventh and on the tenth.
A new game still says only 'Game started. Defend your dream home from the hurdles.', and resuming from a pause or the pin coming back says nothing new.
steps.scenario_name: Moving up to the <wave> wave, I hear that I am now at <rung>, in <neighbourhood>

The sentence status.js says when a wave starts after a clear (its 'play' case after 'clear') becomes `Now on the property ladder at ${ladderName(g.level)}. ${neighbourhood(g.level).name}.`, and status.js already imports neighbourhood. Nothing else changes. 'Wave cleared! Moving up the ladder to {rung}.' stays as it is, and the arrival is still one live-region write. The words stay in status.js (DDD-T9's rule: only the mirror says them), so messages.js is unchanged. M1's enabled scenarios (starting a game, the two interruptions, playing again after Country pile) guard the cases that must not change. No unit spec asserts the old sentence. The step doesn't depend on any backdrop step. Remove the outline's @pending (both Examples blocks, 7 runs). Today each run fails at the Then, because the old sentence is heard.
